{{nihongo|'''Niu Shrine'''|丹生神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

It is a historic shrine listed among the nine shrines of Iitaka District in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.

Also, according to stories that rain came when {{ill|Emperor Saga|Q316654|qid=Q316654}} prayed for rain and clear weather came when he prayed for clearing, Niu Daimyōjin is also called a deity of {{ill|Rainmaking (ritual)|ar|رقصة المطر|bg|Призоваване на дъжд|ca|Dansa de la pluja|da|Regnmageri|de|Regenmacherritual|el|Χορός της βροχής|eo|Pluvdancado|es|Danza de la lluvia|eu|Euri-dantza|fa|رقص باران (آیین)|fi|Sadetanssi|fr|Danse de la pluie|he|ריקוד גשם|hr|Ples za prizivanje kiše|hu|Esőtánc|id|Tari hujan|it|Danza della pioggia|ja|雨乞い|ko|기우제|lt|Lietaus šokis|nl|Regendans|pt|Dança da chuva|ro|Dansul ploii|ru|Обряд вызывания дождя|scn|Abballata di l'acqua di celu|simple|Rain dance|sv|Regndans|tg|Боронхоҳӣ|th|การขอฝน|tr|Yağmur yağdırma|trv|Waya lmawa quyux|uk|Обряд викликання дощу|vi|Cầu mưa|wuu|祈雨舞|zh|祈雨舞|qid=Q477738|lt=praying for rain}} and fair weather.

In the medieval period, the {{ill|Kitabatake clan|Q11403853|qid=Q11403853}} of {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}} worshiped here yearly and supported construction and repairs. Later, a letter of donation was issued by Furuta Daizen, lord of {{ill|Matsusaka Castle|Q1010226|qid=Q1010226}}, donating 30 koku in {{ill|1611|Q6768|qid=Q6768}} ({{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 16). In the same year, Higaki Chikuzen, gon-negi of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|Q11633343|qid=Q11633343|lt=Ise Outer Shrine}}, also served as this shrine’s priest, and thereafter the Higaki line became priests (different from today).

In {{ill|1619|Q6804|qid=Q6804}} ({{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245}} 5), {{ill|Tokugawa Yorinobu|Q1045763|qid=Q1045763}} of the {{ill|Kishū Domain|Q1069187|qid=Q1069187}} recognized 30 koku of {{ill|Jisha-ryō|Q11458058|qid=Q11458058|lt=shrine lands}}. Later domain lords personally visited, prayed for state peace and abundant harvests, and donated gold and silver. In {{ill|1605|Q6741|qid=Q6741}} (An'ei 5), it came under direct control of the Kishū-domain temple-and-shrine magistrate and the {{ill|keidai|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002}} became tax-exempt land. There were also periods when, from {{ill|1677|Q7631|qid=Q7631}} ({{ill|Enpō|fa|انپو|fr|Ère Enpō|ja|延宝|ko|엔포|ru|Эмпо|simple|Enpō|sr|Енпо|sv|Enpō|tr|Enpō|zh|延寶|qid=Q1145735}} 5), old shrine timber from {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|abstract|Q687168|ar|ضريح إيسه|ca|Santuari d'Ise|cs|Svatyně Ise|de|Ise-jingū|el|Μεγάλο Ιερό της Ίσε|eo|Ise-Sanktejo|es|Santuario de Ise|eu|Ise santutegi handia|fa|معبد ایسه|fi|Ise-jingū|fr|Sanctuaire d'Ise|he|מקדש איסה|hu|Iszei nagyszentély|id|Kuil Besar Ise|it|Santuario di Ise|ja|伊勢神宮|ka|ისე-ძინგუ|ko|이세 신궁|ky|Исе ибадатканасы|la|Ise Magnum Templum|lfn|Santeria de Ise|lv|Ises svētnīca|min|Kuil Gadang Ise|ml|ഐസ് ഗ്രാൻഡ് ക്ഷേത്രം|nl|Ise Jingu|no|Ise Jingū|or|ଇଶେ ମହାଶାଳ|pl|Ise-jingū|pt|Santuário de Ise|ru|Храм Исэ|sh|Veliko svetište Ise|simple|Ise Grand Shrine|sl|Veliko svetišče Ise|sv|Ise Jingū|th|ศาลเจ้าอิเซะ|tok|tomo sewi suli Ise|tr|Ise Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ісе|vi|Thần cung Ise|zh|伊势神宫|zh_min_nan|Ise Sîn-kiong|qid=Q687168}} after each {{ill|Sengū|de|Sengū|ja|遷宮|qid=Q2271023}} was granted and used for rebuilding.

On January 21, Meiji 41, more than ten precinct shrines were {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|ja|合祀|qid=Q11412524}}.

Relics related to mercury are preserved together with nearby {{ill|Jingū-ji Temple|ja|神宮寺 (三重県多気町)|qid=Q11589471|lt=Jingū-ji}}, suggesting a deep relation through mercury.

=== Precinct shrines and notable places ===
* Niu-Naka Shrine - deities: {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|es|Kanayamahiko y Kanayamahime|ja|金山彦神|pl|Kanayamahiko|zh|金山毘古神|qid=Q4387856|lt=Kanayamahiko-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kanayamahime-no-Mikoto}}, and 17 others
One of the nine Iitaka District shrines in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō. It is recorded in sources such as old records of Ise Outer Shrine that much mercury was mined in surrounding mountains in ancient times and offered to the two Ise shrines; this shrine preserves sacred treasures such as mining hammers and channels.

Also, from February 18 to April 18, Meiji 41, over 30 village shrines including Hachiman, Yahashira, Konpira, and Shiogaki Shrines were merged, forming the present arrangement.
* Original Ise-tsubaki tree - The {{ill|Camellia japonica|arz|كاميليا جابونيكا|az|Yapon kameliyası|bg|Обикновена камелия|bn|ক্যামেলিয়া|br|Roz-kamelia|ca|Camèlia|ceb|Camellia japonica|cs|Kamélie japonská|da|Kamelia|de|Japanische Kamelie|eo|Japania kamelio|es|Camellia japonica|et|Jaapani kameelia|eu|Japoniako kamelia|fa|کاملیا ژاپنی|fi|Kamelia|fr|Camélia du Japon|frr|Kameelie|gl|Camelia do Xapón|hak|Sân-chhà-fâ|hsb|Japanska kamelija|hu|Japán kamélia|id|Kayucu jepang|ja|ツバキ|ko|동백나무|koi|Камелия|kv|Камелия|lt|Japoninė kamelija|ml|കാമിലിയ ജാപോനിക|mrj|Камели|no|Kamelia|pl|Kamelia japońska|pt|Camellia japonica|ru|Камелия японская|sl|Japonska kamelija|su|Camellia japonica|sv|Kamelia|th|แต้ฮวย|tr|Japon kamelyası|udm|Камелия|ug|چايگۈل|uk|Камелія японська|uz|Camellia japonica|vi|Sơn trà Nhật Bản|war|Camellia japonica|zh|山茶花|zh_yue|茶花|qid=Q160121}} growing beside the {{ill|Shinto architecture|ar|عمارة الشنتو|de|Japanische Schreinarchitektur|fr|Architecture shinto|he|אדריכלות השינטו|hu|Sintó építészet|id|Arsitektur jinja|it|Architettura shintoista|ja|神社建築|ru|Синтоистская архитектура|simple|Shinto architecture|sl|Šintoistična arhitektura|zh|神社建築|qid=Q3080012}} is traditionally said to be the {{ill|original tree|ja|原木|qid=Q11409660}} of Ise-tsubaki (Taki Town designated natural monument No.1).
